subject.title: [Bug] Agent context window fragmentation during concurrent subagent tool calls

question: Should concurrent child completions remain immediate and completion-ordered, or should OpenClaw introduce a requester-side batch mode that waits and presents results in spawn order?
rationale: Both behaviors are coherent but materially different: immediate push delivery minimizes latency and matches sessions_yield semantics, while spawn-order batching delays fast children and changes orchestration behavior without a demonstrated correlation defect.

options.title: Keep push order
options.body: Retain immediate completion-order delivery and require a current-main trace proving wrong-child association before changing runtime behavior.

options.title: Add explicit batch mode
options.body: Design a requester-side aggregation mode that preserves run identity and emits a deterministic spawn-ordered batch only when explicitly requested.

options.title: Resequence globally
options.body: Buffer all concurrent completions until prior calls finish, accepting added latency and head-of-line blocking for deterministic spawn order.

recommendation.title: Keep push order
recommendation.body: Retain immediate completion-order delivery and require a current-main trace proving wrong-child association before changing runtime behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is recent ownership of the subagent registry and lifecycle boundary where this policy would be implemented.
